title: Finite residue field points are closed in finite-type fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $x\in X$ map to $s\in S$, and let $X_s$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. If $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ is a finite field extension, meaning that $\kappa(x)$ is finite-dimensional as a $\kappa(s)$-vector space [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension], then the point of $X_s$ induced by $x$ is closed in $X_s$.

source.place: Tags 01TE and 01TF: Tag 01TE proves that an algebraic residue-field extension makes the point closed in its fibre; the stated finite extension is algebraic (Tag 01TF gives the converse under locally finite type).

proof.text: Set T = f.fiber (f x) and a = f.asFiberHom x : Spec κ(x) → T. Mathlib asFiberHom_fiberToSpecResidueField identifies a followed by the fibre structure map with Spec.map (f.residueFieldMap x), using residue-field point naturality in the canonical pullback lift. Install the algebra structure coming from this residue field map. FiniteDimensional gives Module.Finite and hence Algebra.FiniteType, so HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff makes this composite locally of finite type. Mathlib locallyOfFiniteType_of_comp then makes a locally of finite type.

proof.text: Base-change stability makes T locally of finite type over Spec κ(f x), so the Mathlib fibre instance gives JacobsonSpace T. The source Spec κ(x) is reduced and has one point. Apply Mathlib isFinite_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_of_jacobsonSpace to conclude IsFinite a.

proof.text: A finite scheme morphism is a closed map, so a.isClosedMap.isClosed_range gives that the image of a is closed in T. Mathlib range_asFiberHom identifies this image with the singleton {f.asFiber x}, which proves the conclusion.
